subject.title: Gateway process alive but event loop frozen — all HTTP requests silently timeout

question: Should OpenClaw handle process-alive Gateway event-loop freezes by adding systemd WatchdogSec/systemd-notify recovery to generated Linux/WSL2 units, or keep this issue focused on diagnostics and root-cause isolation only?
rationale: The remaining choice changes managed-service recovery semantics for Linux/systemd users and needs maintainer-approved upgrade behavior plus live proof; automation cannot decide that policy from source inspection alone.

options.title: Refresh and prove systemd watchdog
options.body: Adopt the watchdog direction, require a conflict-free implementation using the supported notification contract, and prove restart behavior on Linux or WSL2 systemd before closing this issue.

options.title: Keep diagnostics and root-cause only
options.body: Reject default supervisor auto-restart for now and track only the blocking operations and diagnostic gaps that make the freeze possible or opaque.

options.title: Split recovery from root causes
options.body: Use this issue as the broad user report, land watchdog recovery under a focused PR, and keep separate root-cause issues for Feishu, memory, provider HTTP, and embedded-run triggers.

recommendation.title: Refresh and prove systemd watchdog
recommendation.body: Adopt the watchdog direction, require a conflict-free implementation using the supported notification contract, and prove restart behavior on Linux or WSL2 systemd before closing this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest service-supervision and gateway recovery history among the sampled current-main paths.
